FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 15 January 
1990, after the draft finalized by the Photographic Materials Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Chemical Division Council. 

This standard was first published in 1971 covering the sizes and tolerances of positive photographic 
paper ( including postcard material) for general use. 

In this present revision sizes with their tolerances of both black and white and colour photographic paper 
in sheets for general use have been specified. The title of the standard has, therefore, also been modified 
accordingly. 

In the formulation of this standard, assistance has been derived from ISO/DIS 7277.2 Photography — 
Black and white and colour papers in sheets for general use — Dimensions and package marking. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final 
value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )\ The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 6139 : 1990 



Indian Standard 



SIZES OF BLACK AND WHITE AND COLOUR 

PHOTOGRAPHIC PAPER IN SHEETS FOR 

GENERAL USE - SPECIFICATION 

( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the sizes, with their 
tolerances of black and white and colour photo- 
graphic paper in sheets for general use and the 
method of marking packed paper. 

1.2 The term 'general use' means use in amateur, 
commercial and portrait photography and excludes 
specific uses such as documentary reproduction, 
phototypesetting or graphic arts.

shall conform to the dimensions given in Table 1 
against corresonding nominal sizes.

3 DIMENSIONAL STABILITY 

3.1 Dimensions may be altered by a permanent 
ageing shrinkage and by temporary shrinkage or 
swell since they may change with the moisture 
content and the temperature of the atmosphere. 
For non-resin coated paper, which is the less 
stable support, the dimensional variation can 
reach as much as 0*3 percent for a 10 percent 
change in relative humidity. Nevertheless, the 
dimensions at the time of package opening and 
after conditioning to 20 ± 2°C and 50 ± 5 per cent 
relative humidity, should not depart from the 
one at the time of cutting by more than ±0*2 
percent. The conditioning of papers at the 
standard atmospheric conditions requires a mini- 
mum of 4 hours for non-resin coated papers and 
4 days for resin coated papers. 

4 TOLERANCES 

4.1 The tolerances on the actual cutting sizes 
specified in Table 1 shall be as follows:

Greater than 50 cm 

5 SQUARENESS 

5.1 Neither the diagonal of any sheet of paper shall 
exceed the diagonal of a rectangular sheet of the 
appropriate maximum cutting length and width, 
nor shall it be less than the diagonal of a rectangular 
sheet of the appropriate minimum length and 
width.

Bureau of Indian Standards 



BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standard Act , 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any from without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type of grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary andf amendments, if any, are 
issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of 
the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent in BIS giving the 
following reference :
